messages.subject: Query about coding Capture-recapture-Recovery data
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to estimate the survival, capture, and recovery rate, where an individual is captured then may or may not recaptured. If it is dead, it may or may not be recovered.

Here is my code with sample data:

library(nimble)
library(tidyverse)

# Sample data matrix (0 -> Not Observed, 1 -> Captured, 2 -> Recovered)
y <- matrix(c(
  1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0,
  1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0,
  1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0,
  1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2,
  1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0
), nrow = 5, byrow = TRUE)

# Define the first capture occasions
first <- apply(y, 1, function(row) min(which(row != 0)))

# Add 1 to convert y to a form suitable for Nimble (N=1, C=2, R=3)
my.data <- list(y = y + 1)

nyears <- ncol(y)
N <- nrow(y)

# Initialize K array with the last time point of the study
K <- rep(ncol(y), nrow(y))

# Update K with the last time point when the observation is 2
for (i in 1:N) {
  last_recovered <- max(which(y[i, ] == 2), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (last_recovered != -Inf) {
    K[i] <- last_recovered
  }
}
# Define constants for Nimble
my.constants <- list(first = first,
                     K = K,
                     N = N)

# Generate initial values for the latent states
zinits <- matrix(1, N, nyears)  # Set to 1 or another appropriate value for initial state
for (i in 1:N) {
  if (first[i] > 1) zinits[i, 1:(first[i]-1)] <- NA
}

# Ensure that zinits reflect the initial observations
for (i in 1:N) {
  zinits[i, first[i]] <- y[i, first[i]]  # Initial states based on first observation
}

initial.values <- function() {
  list(phi = runif(1, 0, 1),
       lambda = runif(1, 0, 1),
       p = runif(1, 0, 1),
       z = zinits)
}

# Define the model code
code_m <- nimbleCode({
 
  # priors
  phi ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  lambda ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  p ~ dbeta(1, 1)
 
  # probabilities of state z(t+1) given z(t)
  gamma[1,1] <- phi
  gamma[1,2] <- 1 - phi
  gamma[2,1] <- 0
  gamma[2,2] <- 1
 
  # probabilities of y(t) given z(t)
  omega[1,1] <- 1-p
  omega[1,2] <- p
  omega[1,3] <- 0
  omega[2,1] <- 1-lambda
  omega[2,2] <- 0
  omega[2,3] <- lambda
 
  # likelihood
  for (i in 1:N){
    # latent state at first capture
    z[i,first[i]] <- y[i,first[i]] - 1
    for (t in (first[i]+1):K[i]){
      # draw z(t) given z(t-1)
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,t-1], 1:2])
      # draw y(t) given z(t)
      y[i,t] ~ dcat(omega[z[i,t], 1:3])
    }
  }
})

# Parameters to monitor
parameters.to.save <- c("phi", "p", "lambda")

# MCMC settings
n.iter <- 100
n.burnin <- 20
n.chains <- 3

# Run the MCMC
mcmc.multistate <- nimbleMCMC(code = code_m,
                              constants = my.constants,
                              data = my.data,              
                              inits = initial.values(),
                              monitors = parameters.to.save,
                              niter = n.iter,
                              nburnin = n.burnin,
                              nchains = n.chains,
                              summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE)

-----------------------------
Now, the error I am getting is :
[Note] Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_y. running chain 1... warning: logProb of data node y[3, 3]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[8, 4]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[4, 5]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[5, 4]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[1, 5]: logProb is -Inf. |-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------| |-------------------------------------------------------|
----------------------------------
My question is, how should I solve this? or is it okay to get this warning? I found it is still working and giving me estimates. Or, Is there any better way to model with recovery data?

Thank you so much,
Arjun
--

messages.author: a4c5d7d1c977b688
messages.subject: Re: Query about coding Capture-recapture-Recovery data
parts:
Hi Arjun,

Giving z better initial values solves the problem:

# Generate initial values for the latent states
zinits <- matrix(1, N, nyears)  # Set to 1 or another appropriate value for initial state
for (i in 1:N) {
  if (first[i] > 1) zinits[i, 1:(first[i]-1)] <- NA

if (length(which(y[i,]==2)) == 1) {
    zinits[i,which(y[i,]==2):7] <- 2
  }
}

I guess the warning probably doesn't matter. However, over the years I found it a good idea to give z reasonable initial values. Hope that helps.

Best,
Qing
